review.recommendation: Full jitter and the injectable `random` hook are the right approach, but the rewritten loop introduces an off-by-one: `for (attempt = 0; attempt <= opts.attempts; ...)` calls `fn` up to `attempts + 1` times, directly violating the provider's 3-attempt cap (a caller passing attempts:3 now makes a 4th call → merchant throttling) and contradicting the unchanged JSDoc 'at most `attempts` times in total'. It also sleeps after the final failure and changes the `attempts: 0` edge case from 'never call' to 'call once'. Restore `attempt < opts.attempts` with the sleep condition `attempt < opts.attempts - 1`, keeping jitter, `Math.round`, and the `random` hook; then add a test using a stubbed `random` (e.g. `() => 0.5`) asserting `fn` is invoked exactly `attempts` times and the last delay is `base * 2**(attempts-1)`.
critical_assumptions: `opts.attempts` means total invocations of `fn` (per the JSDoc), and callers map it directly to the provider's 'at most 3 attempts per charge' rule (i.e., someone passes attempts: 3).
Existing tests in test/retry.test.js assert exact call counts and/or sleep sequences.
Sleeping after the final failed attempt has no downstream value (no webhook/poll on the last delay) — true under the original semantics.
material_risks: One extra charge attempt per failure sequence triggers provider-side throttling of the merchant account — the exact incident class the constraint exists to prevent.
Silent behavioral break for every retry() caller (chargeWithRetry and others) without any signature change, so no type/lint signal; only runtime tests would catch it.
With the buggy loop, `attempts: 0` now invokes `fn` once instead of zero times, and `throw lastError` can still propagate `undefined` for `attempts <= 0`.
Extra sleep after the last allowed failure delays error surfacing/payment failure reporting by up to base*2^(attempts-1) ms.
